source.title_or_context: **Recommendation Table 7 — Recommendations for evaluation of relatives of sudden arrhythmic death syndrome decedents**

table_assessment.assessment_notes: Eight graded familial-evaluation recommendation rows across two ordered table parts. The first row's four list-item applicability clauses are exact separate text units sharing the main row's I/B grade. All remaining recommendation cells and grades are annotated.

normative_assertions.notes: Main recommendation; exact applicability groups/conditions follow in four linked bullet text units.

text_units.verbatim_text: Familial evaluation of SADS decedents is recommended:

normative_assertions.notes: Second applicability bullet; mutation carriage is based on family-history analysis.

text_units.verbatim_text: • for relatives who must carry a mutation based on analysis of the family history

header_path: Familial evaluation of SADS decedents is recommended

normative_assertions.notes: Fourth applicability bullet with age threshold or other evidence suggesting heritable disease.
source_trigger_texts: Familial evaluation of SADS decedents is recommended

text_units.verbatim_text: • when the decedent's age is <50 years, or if there is other circumstantial data or family history to suggest heritable disease.

normative_assertions.notes: Familial evaluation should include genetic testing when post-mortem testing detects a pathogenic mutation.

text_units.verbatim_text: Familial evaluation of SADS decedents is recommended to include genetic testing when post-mortem genetic testing in a SADS decedent detects a pathogenic mutation.

entities.surface_form: standard and high precordial lead ECG

normative_assertions.notes: ASSESS covers the coordinated history, examination, ECG, echocardiography and exercise-testing components.

text_units.verbatim_text: Baseline familial evaluation of SADS decedents is recommended to include taking a medical history and performing physical examination, standard and high precordial lead ECG, echocardiography, and exercise testing.

entities.surface_form: SADS families without a diagnosis after clinical evaluation

normative_assertions.notes: Follow-up continues through adulthood for children in undiagnosed SADS families.

text_units.verbatim_text: In SADS families without a diagnosis after clinical evaluation, follow-up is recommended for children of decedents until they reach adulthood.

entities.surface_form: relatives of SADS decedents who are 16 years or older

normative_assertions.notes: Pharmacological testing applies to the age-defined relative population when baseline/proband findings raise BrS suspicion.

text_units.verbatim_text: Pharmacological testing with a sodium channel blocker should be considered in relatives of SADS decedents who are 16 years or older when baseline testing and/or proband findings increase the suspicion of BrS.

normative_assertions.notes: CMR is the coordinated imaging option.

text_units.verbatim_text: Ambulatory cardiac rhythm monitoring and CMR may be considered in relatives of SADS decedents.

entities.surface_form: first-degree relatives of SADS decedents with normal baseline testing

normative_assertions.notes: Epinephrine challenge is explicitly conditioned on impractical exercise testing; both challenges apply to first-degree relatives with normal baseline testing.

text_units.verbatim_text: Pharmacological testing including epinephrine challenge (if exercise testing is impractical) and sodium channel blocker challenge may be considered in first-degree relatives of SADS decedents with normal baseline testing.

entities.surface_form: SADS families without a diagnosis after clinical evaluation

normative_assertions.notes: Routine follow-up is against for asymptomatic adults in undiagnosed SADS families.
Return is conditionally advised if symptoms develop or family history changes.

text_units.verbatim_text: In SADS families without a diagnosis after clinical evaluation, follow-up is not recommended for asymptomatic adults who can be discharged with advice to return if they develop symptoms or if the family history changes.
